editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with nothing missing. It uses "valoarea așteptată"/"valorile așteptate" consistently for expectation value and "atenuarea erorilor" for error mitigation, and SLC's "delimita mai strict sensibilitatea la erori" matches "more tightly bound" exactly.

The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The pre-flight checks, error mitigation (TEM/PEC) and circuit/application function passages match the English, and the terms are consistent: atenuarea erorilor, transpilare, qubiți, shot-uri. There are three small wording slips. In [63] "utility-grade performance" becomes "performanță la scară utilitară (utility-scale)", which swaps "grade" for "scale" and uses a stiff calque. In [66] "contribuite de" is an anglicism. In [34] the singular "un tip de reactor nuclear" is followed by the plural "reactoare modulare mici", which is a number mismatch.

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box
examples.translation: pentru a oferi direct, fără configurare suplimentară, performanță la scară utilitară (utility-scale)
examples.suggested: pentru a oferi, direct și fără configurare suplimentară, performanță la nivel de utilitate (utility-grade)
examples.why: The source says utility-grade, not utility-scale. The gloss swaps the concept, and "scară utilitară" reads as a calque.

examples.suggested: funcții oferite / dezvoltate de partenerii noștri
examples.why: "contribuite" is an anglicism a native technical editor would replace.

examples.source: a type of nuclear reactor known as Small Modular Reactors
examples.translation: într-un tip de reactor nuclear cunoscut sub numele de reactoare modulare mici
examples.suggested: într-un tip de reactor nuclear cunoscut sub numele de reactor modular mic (Small Modular Reactor, SMR)
examples.why: The singular "un tip de reactor" clashes with the plural name that follows, so the sentence reads awkwardly.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It renders "skills" consistently as "abilitățile Qiskit" and "changelog" as "Jurnal de modificări", and [5] ("A fost lansată abilitatea ... destinată migrării codului") keeps the English meaning exactly.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps the hedge in [9] ("might be faster" → "ar putea fi mai rapide"); key terms are rendered correctly ("AI-powered transpiler passes" → "treceri de transpilare ... bazate pe AI", "changelog" → "Jurnalul de modificări"), and it uses the informal "tu" register throughout ("Consultă", "vizitează", "Citește").

The translation is faithful overall, uses the informal "tu" register ("Scrie", "Vizitează", "Te întrebi") and renders terms correctly ("qubiți", "transpilare", "tolerant la erori", "pipeline"). In the [11] heading, "transpilarea timpurie tolerantă la erori" attaches "early" to the transpilation. The source means transpilation for early fault-tolerant targets, and the body text gets this right. The opening [6] is a stiff calque ("Bazându-se pe avântul stabilit"). In [10], "comună" is used for both "joint" and "common", which is ambiguous.

examples.translation: Îmbunătățiri în transpilarea timpurie tolerantă la erori
examples.suggested: Îmbunătățiri în transpilarea pentru sisteme timpurii tolerante la erori
examples.why: In the Romanian, 'timpurie' describes the transpilation instead of the early fault-tolerant hardware. The body text clarifies this, so it is minor.

examples.source: Building on the momentum established across the v2.x series
examples.translation: Bazându-se pe avântul stabilit pe parcursul seriei v2.x
examples.why: A word-for-word calque of the English idiom. A native technical writer would not say 'avânt stabilit'.

examples.source: enables joint projective measurement ... a common representation
examples.translation: permite măsurarea proiectivă comună ... o reprezentare comună
examples.suggested: măsurarea proiectivă conjunctă ... o reprezentare des folosită
examples.why: 'comună' is used for both 'joint' and 'common' in the same sentence. 'conjunctă' is the clearer term for a joint measurement.

editor_note: I found no meaning drift. Dates, quantities (1 µs vs 250 µs, 68 vs 138 ns, 20-2000 µs, 57 of 176 gates) and caveats such as the ibm_berlin/ibm_miami limitations are all kept faithfully. Several terms are rendered inconsistently. "Gate" is sometimes left as "gate-uri" ([29], [56], [86], [122]) and sometimes translated as "porți" ([178], [180], [258], [272], [280]). "Job" appears as both "job-uri" and "joburi". The Gen3 "engine stack" is "stack-ul de motor" in [262] but "stiva motorului" in [272]. "Utility scale" is "scară de utilitate" in [163] but "scară utilitară" in [99]. The UI labels Compute resources and Instance access are left in English in [114]/[116] but translated as "Resurse de calcul" and "Acces la instanță" in [145]/[146]. A few phrases are also stiff calques, for example "aproximativ de 5x mai mici EPLG" and "practice pentru rulare de rutină".

examples.source: 57 of 176 possible two-qubit gates below the 1e-3 error level
examples.translation: cu 57 din 176 de gate-uri cu doi qubiți posibile
examples.suggested: cu 57 din 176 de porți cu doi qubiți posibile (choose one: porți or gate-uri, and use it throughout)
examples.why: The same term is "porți" in [178], [180], [258] and [280], so the file mixes the English and Romanian forms.

examples.why: [262] calls the same thing "stack-ul de motor Gen3", and "stiva motorului" reads like a literal calque.

examples.suggested: Poți în continuare filtra tabelul Compute resources după regiune
examples.why: [114] leaves the UI label untranslated ("Compute resources"), so this entry is inconsistent with it. The UI labels themselves are in English.

examples.source: approximately 5x lower EPLG) and faster gates (nearly 8x faster)
examples.translation: (aproximativ de 5x mai mici EPLG) și porți mai rapide (aproape de 8x mai rapide)
examples.suggested: (un EPLG de aproximativ 5 ori mai mic) și porți de aproape 8 ori mai rapide
examples.why: The word order is calqued from English and the agreement is awkward. A native writer would say "de N ori mai mic".
